newsitem.title: USA: IFC adds Russia, four other countries to key index.
newsitem.headline: IFC adds Russia, four other countries to key index.

text.p: The International Finance Corp (IFC) said on Tuesday it would add Russia and four other countries to one of its key stock indices to give investors a broader view of the world's emerging markets.

Russia, Israel, Egypt, Morocco and Slovakia will be added to the IFC investable composite index beginning November 3, increasing the number of countries the index covers to 31, the IFC, the private-sector affiliate of the World Bank, said.
"These are new and exciting countries for global investors," said Robert Shakotko, manager of the IFC's emerging markets index group.
He said the IFC decided to add the five countries to the index because the stock markets in each have become more accessible to foreign investors.
"Investor interest has been strong, and we expect the addition of these five new countries to the (investable composite index) to reinforce that interest," he said.
The IFC said its goal was to increase the flow of private capital into the five countries by giving investors more information about their leading companies and the state of their economies.
Many emerging markets funds use the IFC index to track the performance of emerging markets in areas where it is difficult to invest.
In some of these countries, shares are tightly held or opaque legislation deters investors or makes it hard to repatriate profits.
Shakotko said the countries added to the index would benefit over time. "It's going to mean direct investments in these five countries," he said. "It's very tangible."

The IFC said Russian stocks would have a 2.9 percent weight in its investable composite index, Israel would have 1.8 percent, Egypt 0.6, Morocco 0.5 percent and Slovakia 0.1 percent. The weights will change depending on market conditions in each of the countries, the IFC said.

Russia, Egypt and Morocco are already included in IFC's global composite index, which tracks market performance with fewer restrictions. Israel and Slovakia have never before been included in an IFC composite index.
